newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 3-mth CD rate 0.58 pct, highest since Aug 23.
newsitem.headline: Japan 3-mth CD rate 0.58 pct, highest since Aug 23.

text.p: Japan's long-term money market benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate rose to 0.58 percent on Friday morning, its highest since August 23, 1996, money traders said.
Three-month CDs were last issued at 0.55 percent on Tuesday.
Traders said the rise in the CD rate was due to strong bank demand for funds covering the fiscal year-end on March 31.
"Compared with three-month Euroyen cash rates, which were around 0.64-0.65 percent this morning, the 0.58 percent level was still attractive for CD issuers," said a city bank dealer.

The short-end key overnight call rate stood at 0.53 percent on Friday morning, up from Wednesday's 0.51, due to seasonally strong fund demand ahead of March 31, traders said. The Tokyo financial markets were closed on Thursday for a holiday.
